stories.head: Russian barrage kills eight in Ukraine as objects cross into Poland
stories.say: Russia fired hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles at Ukraine overnight into Friday, killing at least eight people, while Poland said two missiles and a drone crossed its airspace.
stories.stand: Kyiv's bridges, water and power were hit after Vladimir Putin vowed a painful response to Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean bridge.
body: Russia launched a large overnight attack on Ukraine into Friday, killing at least eight people, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Ukrainian officials. Zelenskyy said more than 400 drones were used.

Kyiv authorities said three employees were killed in a strike on a water utility. Three bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv were hit, and attacks on electricity infrastructure caused widespread blackouts. Two people were killed at a railway station in Lviv.

Poland's defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, said three objects, likely two missiles and a drone, violated Polish airspace. No injuries were reported. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation, and Poland scrambled fighter jets.
Some Russian weapons hit the Austrian embassy in Kyiv. France called for a UN Security Council meeting, and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte called the incident clearly dangerous.

stories.head: Denmark expels Russian attaché over alleged plot to kill rapper
stories.say: Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attaché, saying its intelligence service suspects Moscow planned to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a concert near Copenhagen in September.
stories.stand: Danish intelligence suspects Russia planned to assassinate the Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at a September concert; Moscow calls the move vengeful.
body: Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attaché. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said the diplomat must leave within seven days.

The intelligence service PET suspects Russia planned to assassinate the Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at a concert in a Copenhagen suburb on 25 September. Three people were stopped near the venue, and police found firearms and knives. The concert was cancelled.
Two Danish men have been charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service. Police and PET suspect a banned gang helped plan the attack.
The Russian embassy called the expulsion vengeful and said Denmark had presented no evidence of Russian involvement.

stories.head: Estonia to close all road crossings with Russia from 1 December
stories.say: Estonia will shut its road border crossings with Russia for at least six months from the first of December, after an attempted arson attack it blames on Russian military intelligence.
stories.stand: Tallinn blames Russian military intelligence for an attempted arson attack on a drone maker; Moscow calls the closure a new Iron Curtain.
body: Estonia's government has approved closing its road border crossings with Russia from Tuesday 1 December. The closure is set for six months and may be extended. Rail freight is not affected.

Estonian authorities say Russian military intelligence ordered an attempted arson attack on the drone maker Threod Systems near Tallinn on 14 November. Production was not damaged, and eight people from Latvia were detained.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal said Estonia would not let Russia use its openness against it. The Kremlin denied involvement, and Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova compared the move to a new Iron Curtain.

stories.head: Myanmar calls UN court's Rohingya genocide ruling unfair
stories.say: Myanmar's government has rejected Thursday's International Court of Justice ruling that it committed genocide against the Rohingya, calling it unfair. China also criticised the decision.
stories.stand: The court found Myanmar responsible for genocide in 2017 by nine votes to six; Myanmar and China both objected on Friday.
body: Myanmar has rejected the International Court of Justice ruling that it committed genocide against its Rohingya minority in 2017. Government spokesperson Khaing Khaing Soe said the country had been unjustly accused and noted the decision was not unanimous.

Nine of the court's 15 judges backed the genocide finding. It is the first time the court has found a state responsible for genocide. The judges found mass executions, widespread sexual violence and hundreds of villages burned.

The court ordered Myanmar to pay compensation, with amounts set later, and to allow displaced Rohingya to return safely. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said such rulings are not conducive to settling disputes.

stories.say: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh, the third night in a row of emergency alerts in the Saudi capital.
stories.stand: The coalition also says it struck the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah and Sanaa, as both sides threaten each other's ports.
body: The Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen's government, said it intercepted three ballistic missiles heading for Riyadh. Saudi Arabia issued emergency alerts for the capital and lifted them soon after, for the third night running.
Two days earlier, Houthi missiles hit the Public Investment Fund skyscraper in Riyadh. The coalition said it had struck the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah and Sanaa.
The Houthis have threatened a Saudi power station, Red Sea ports including Jeddah, and Riyadh's financial centre.

stories.head: US and Israel weighing new strikes on Iran, CBS sources say
stories.say: Israel and the United States are weighing a new short-term assault on Iran, according to sources cited by CBS News. Donald Trump says he is not rushing into any decision.
stories.stand: Israel is said to worry about Iran rebuilding missile production; Tehran rejects Trump's claim that it may be seeking chemical or biological weapons.
body: Israel and the United States are considering a new short-term assault on Iran, according to sources cited by CBS News. Israel is said to prefer a joint operation but is unsure whether Donald Trump will order one.
Israeli officials are reported to be concerned that Iran is rebuilding ballistic missile production and moving nuclear sites underground.

Trump has said Iran may be seeking chemical or biological weapons, without offering evidence. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baqaei, rejected the claims. Trump told Israel's Channel 12 he was not rushing into any decision.

stories.head: Boat carrying mourners capsizes in Nigeria, killing at least four
stories.say: At least four people, including two children, died when an overcrowded boat taking mourners to a funeral capsized in Nigeria's Bayelsa State on Friday, police said.
stories.stand: Police say 24 people were rescued and the search continues; residents told Reuters at least 300 people were on board.
body: An overcrowded boat carrying mourners to a funeral capsized in Bayelsa State, southern Nigeria, on Friday. Police said at least four people died, two adults and two children.
Police spokesperson Musa Mohammed said the boat suffered a mechanical failure. Twenty-four people were rescued, and search teams are still looking for more victims.
Police did not say how many were on board. Some residents told Reuters at least 300 people were. The driver fled, and the vessel's manager has been taken into custody.

stories.head: Belgrade mayor charged with assaulting opposition councillor
stories.say: Serbian prosecutors have charged Belgrade's mayor, Aleksandar Sapic, with seriously injuring an opposition councillor during a row in September. He denies attacking her.
stories.stand: Prosecutors seek a three-year sentence for Aleksandar Sapic, a senior figure in the Serbian Progressive Party; he says he scuffled only with her husband.
body: Prosecutors in Serbia on Friday charged Belgrade Mayor Aleksandar Sapic with assaulting opposition councillor Tatjana Micic during an argument in September.
Prosecutors allege Sapic grabbed Micic's arm and punched her in the face, causing fractures they describe as grievous bodily harm. They are seeking a three-year sentence.
Sapic denies attacking Micic but admits a scuffle with her husband. Opposition parties have demanded his resignation, which he has refused.

stories.head: Hungary to lift veto on Ukraine's remaining EU accession talks
stories.say: Hungary is set to drop its objections to Ukraine's last two blocks of EU membership talks, diplomats told Euronews, which would let Kyiv and Moldova open every chapter.
stories.stand: The shift follows Péter Magyar's defeat of Viktor Orbán; member states can still veto progress many more times.
body: Hungary will lift its objections to Ukraine's final two EU accession negotiating clusters, two diplomatic sources told Euronews. The decision was expected at a meeting of EU ambassadors on Friday.
That would let Ukraine and Moldova open all clusters, including environment and agriculture. Moldova's bid is linked to Kyiv's.
The change follows Péter Magyar ousting Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power. Member states can still veto progress more than 100 times before membership.

stories.head: Rio Tinto pledges $370m to tackle Panguna mine legacy
stories.say: Rio Tinto will put three hundred and seventy million dollars into a fund to deal with the damage left by the Panguna copper mine in Bougainville, closed since nineteen eighty-nine.
stories.stand: An assessment found mine waste and decaying infrastructure affect thousands; landowners say clean water is the priority.
body: Rio Tinto says it will voluntarily contribute $370m over coming years to a new fund to address the impacts of the Panguna mine in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea.
The mine closed in 1989 after local opposition, sparking the Bougainville Crisis. An impact assessment found that mine waste and decaying infrastructure affect thousands of people.
The assessment followed a 2020 complaint by the Human Rights Law Centre. Lead complainant Theonila Roka Matbob said clean water and transport are immediate priorities.

stories.say: Rallies took place across twenty-five European countries on Friday over living costs, wages and military spending, with a general strike in Italy and clashes in Bologna.
stories.stand: France counted 146,000 protesters nationwide, while the CGT union claimed just over 500,000.
body: Rallies were held in 25 European countries on Friday, including the UK, Germany, Spain, Italy and Austria, over living costs, wages, public services and military spending.

stories.head: Temperatures fall to -8.4C in Scotland on coldest night of autumn
stories.say: Temperatures fell to minus eight point four degrees in the Scottish Highlands on Thursday night, the coldest of the autumn, with harsh frost and freezing fog expected through the weekend.
stories.stand: Forecasters expect lows near -9C in Scotland and cold health alerts cover northern England until Monday.
body: Thursday night was the coldest of the autumn so far, with temperatures falling to -8.4C at Tulloch Bridge in the Scottish Highlands and -4.9C at Shap in Cumbria, ITV News reported.

Lows of about -9C were forecast in Scotland on Friday night, with deep frost and freezing fog likely in parts of Scotland and central and eastern England. Ice may form on untreated surfaces in rural areas.
Cold nights are expected to continue through the weekend. The UK Health Security Agency has cold health alerts in place for northern England until Monday morning.

stories.head: Calls grow to change consent law after Young abuse convictions
stories.say: There are growing calls to update consent laws after four men were convicted of sexually abusing Joanne Young, who had been drugged by her husband over thirteen years.
stories.stand: Joanne Young said no one should be able to give consent on someone else's behalf; Jess Phillips says online safety laws must be reinforced.
body: Calls are growing for consent laws to be changed after four men were convicted at Winchester Crown Court on Thursday of sexual offences against Joanne Young.
Her husband, Philip Young, drugged and raped her over 13 years at their home in Swindon and recruited the men online. He pleaded guilty to 56 charges.

Speaking outside court, Joanne Young said no one should be able to give consent on someone else's behalf. Minister Jess Phillips told LBC that online safety laws must be reinforced. The charity Refuge warned the case was not a standalone one.

body: The fishing vessel Kilda has been found partially sunk off Orkney and taken to Kirkwall on Thursday evening, Police Scotland said.
Three people were on board when it went missing off the Isle of Lewis on 13 October. One crew member was found dead the next day, and two have not been found.
Inspector Neil Taylor confirmed the vessel was the FV Kilda. Police will examine it, working with the Marine Accident Investigation Branch and the Maritime and Coastguard Agency.

stories.say: Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo, was due to be sentenced at Portsmouth Crown Court on Friday for slashing a migrant dinghy in the Channel.
stories.stand: He pleaded guilty to criminal damage last week; the maximum sentence is three months in prison.
body: Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo, was due to be sentenced at Portsmouth Crown Court on Friday for criminal damage.
He slashed a migrant dinghy with a knife in the English Channel on 22 September. He initially denied the charge but pleaded guilty last week, and has been in custody for eight weeks.
The maximum sentence for criminal damage under £5,000 is three months in prison and or a fine, according to the Sentencing Council. Thomas is an associate of Tommy Robinson.

stories.head: Driver jailed after 137mph crash that killed friend
stories.say: A man who inhaled nitrous oxide before driving at a hundred and thirty-seven miles an hour in Kent, killing a nineteen-year-old passenger, has been jailed for eleven years and nine months.
stories.stand: Luciano Spirito, 25, from Bromley, pleaded guilty; three other passengers were hurt.
body: Luciano Spirito, 25, of Bromley, has been jailed for 11 years and 9 months after a crash on the A20 near Farningham in Kent in February 2023, Kent Police said.
A 19-year-old passenger was killed and three others were injured. CCTV showed Spirito inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon before he got into the driver's seat.
He initially denied the charges but later pleaded guilty. He was banned from driving for eight years from his release.

stories.head: Nuclear submarine HMS Vengeance ends record 217-day patrol
stories.say: The nuclear submarine HMS Vengeance has returned to Scotland after a record two hundred and seventeen days on patrol, and experts warn longer missions reflect delayed maintenance.
stories.stand: The Vanguard-class boats were designed for missions of about three months and about 25 years of service.
body: HMS Vengeance, one of Britain's four Vanguard-class nuclear submarines, has returned to Scotland after a 217-day deployment, Euronews reported. That beats the 205-day record set by HMS Vanguard in April.
Experts link longer patrols to delayed maintenance on ageing submarines and strain on crews. A submarine specialist told The Guardian the boats were designed for missions of about three months.
The Vanguard boats were designed for about 25 years of service but are expected to run for about 40. Their replacement, HMS Dreadnought, is expected around 2032.

stories.stand: HMRC seized more than 1.4 million cigarettes, 5.5 tonnes of tobacco, cash and gold bars.
body: HM Revenue and Customs has dismantled a fully working illegal cigarette factory at an industrial site in Bourne, Lincolnshire, after a fraud investigation.
HMRC said the factory could make more than 200,000 cigarettes a day. Officers seized more than 1.4 million cigarettes and about 5.5 tonnes of tobacco, along with £645,000 in cash and four gold bars.
Twenty-one people were arrested on suspicion of excise duty evasion and released pending further inquiries.

stories.stand: The doctors criticised the police response; a local MP called it a national crisis and an anti-racism march is planned for Saturday.
body: Four British doctors, three from ethnic minority backgrounds, say they were attacked and racially abused outside a pub in Chichester, ITV News reported. Two teenage girls are alleged to have carried out the attack.
The doctors accuse Sussex Police of handling the case poorly. The force says its response did not reflect the service it aims to provide and that a thorough investigation is under way.

Home Office data show race hate crimes in England and Wales rose 9% over the past year. Chichester's Liberal Democrat MP, Jess Brown-Fuller, called it a national crisis. An anti-racism march is planned in the city on Saturday.

stories.say: Eight more hotels housing asylum seekers will close in December, leaving about a hundred and forty in use, though a Conservative MP calls the closures smoke and mirrors.
stories.stand: Hotel numbers are down from 213 at the 2024 election; critics question moves to large sites.
body: Eight hotels housing asylum seekers in the UK will close in December, leaving about 140 in use, down from 213 at the 2024 election, ITV News reported. Hotels in Hove, Aldershot, Crawley and Bournemouth are among those closing.
Minister Anna Turley credited the government's reforms for fewer small boat arrivals.

Conservative MP Gregory Stafford called the closures smoke and mirrors, saying people were being moved to other large sites. Liberal Democrat MP Alison Bennett opposed moving people to derelict military sites.

stories.stand: Prosecutors allege George Gordon killed a friend in 2023 and kept her body in a chest freezer; the trial resumes on Monday.
body: George Gordon, 65, is on trial at Liverpool Crown Court accused of murdering a friend in St Helens in April 2023. He denies murder and a charge of causing unnecessary suffering to animals.

Prosecutors allege he kept the woman's body in a chest freezer for almost three years. Jurors were told body-worn camera footage captured him saying she was in the freezer as he was led out of his flat in January.
Gordon was absent on Thursday, reportedly unwell. The trial resumes on Monday.

stories.head: Burnham agrees UK-EU deals on food, carbon and youth mobility
stories.say: Andy Burnham has agreed new deals with the EU in Brussels, cutting checks on food exports, linking carbon markets and letting a hundred thousand young people a year live on either side.
stories.stand: Burnham says the deals could add 0.5% to GDP; tuition fees are unresolved and both parliaments must still approve.
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham agreed a package of deals with EU leaders at a summit in Brussels on Friday, meeting Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa.
The deals would remove routine border checks on food and farm exports, link the UK and EU emissions trading schemes, and create a youth scheme for up to 100,000 young people from each side.

body: Researchers at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, led by Professor Gabriele Macho, have re-examined the Taung Child, found in South Africa in 1924, ScienceDaily reported.

body: The London Ambulance Service has declared a critical incident after days of sustained high demand. Calls topped 7,300 a day on three consecutive days from Monday 16 November.

body: MEPs and EU governments struck a provisional deal overnight into Thursday to delay EU methane emissions rules by two years, Euronews reported.

The 2024 rules require foreign suppliers to report methane emissions linked to oil, gas and coal sold to EU buyers. Importers' monitoring and reporting duties move from January 2027 to 1 January 2029.
The compromise is shorter than the three-year delay the Parliament backed in October. Critics say it favours the oil and gas industry. Formal approval is needed by the end of the year.

stories.head: Drone operator apologises for filming Pochettino's first United session
stories.say: A drone operator has apologised and removed footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first Manchester United training session, calling it a total error of judgement.
stories.stand: He says the flight was legal and denies any rival club was involved; United face Liverpool on Sunday.
body: A drone operator who filmed Manchester United's training at Carrington has removed the footage and apologised, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters. The session on Thursday was Mauricio Pochettino's first as manager.
In a statement on Friday, the operator called the filming unethical and a total error of judgement, but said the flight was legal. He denied that Liverpool or any other club had influenced him.
United are 18th after one win in 10 league games and play Liverpool on Sunday.

stories.head: Australian government urges openness in ball-tampering forum
stories.say: Australia's government has urged Cricket Australia to run its forum on the twenty eighteen ball-tampering scandal as independently and openly as possible, after new claims about who knew.
stories.stand: Usman Khawaja alleges others knew; Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc deny prior knowledge.
body: Australia's government has urged Cricket Australia to run its forum on the 2018 ball-tampering scandal as independently and openly as possible, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters.
The forum lets players give their accounts, but the results may not be published and no sanctions will follow.
Usman Khawaja has alleged that other players and staff knew about the plan. Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc deny prior knowledge. Cameron Bancroft said the whole team knew.

stories.head: Tashima says Balogun red card row drove his FIFA bid
stories.say: Japan's Kozo Tashima says FIFA's handling of Folarin Balogun's red card at the World Cup prompted him to stand against Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency.
stories.stand: FIFA suspended Balogun's ban after Donald Trump asked Infantino to review it; the election is in March 2027.
body: Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association, says the handling of Folarin Balogun's red card at the World Cup prompted his bid for the FIFA presidency, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters.

FIFA suspended Balogun's automatic one-match ban in July, letting the US striker play Belgium, after Donald Trump asked Gianni Infantino to review it. FIFA says it will amend the rule that allowed this.
Tashima faces Infantino and Philippe Diallo in the March 2027 election.
